definition: Fine-tuning smaller models on long-CoT traces sampled from a strong reasoning teacher, transferring much of the deliberation behavior without RL.
details: Fine-tuning smaller models on long-CoT traces sampled from a strong reasoning teacher, transferring much of the deliberation behavior without RL. How compact reasoning models are made, and why frontier labs restrict training on their outputs.

explainer.lead: Reasoning distillation fine-tunes smaller models on long chain-of-thought traces from a strong reasoning teacher, transferring deliberation without reinforcement learning. It matters as a way to make compact reasoning models.

tiers.eli5: Like a student learning by studying a expert's fully worked solutions instead of solving everything from scratch.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers sample long CoT traces from a strong teacher and fine-tune a smaller student on them. Pitfall: frontier labs restrict training on their outputs, which limits such data.
tiers.paperLevel: Supervised fine-tuning of a smaller model on long chain-of-thought traces sampled from a stronger reasoning teacher, transferring much of the deliberation behavior without RL. Its effectiveness depends on the quality and availability of teacher traces.

explainer.example: A small model is fine-tuned on step-by-step solutions produced by a large reasoning model and then solves similar problems with its own long traces.
